title: The pig pen job with Steve Lewis
summary: Williams lists who played at Steve Lewis's pig pen and describes Steve's private nasty songs.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: What about this job at the pig pen?
Yeah. Did you have a saxophone, a clarinet, a trombone there?
Let me see now. Let me get that line up together.
I got Steve Albert out, huh?
Steve didn't play. Herbert Richardson. Yeah, I see. Herbert Richardson. Was, did O.L. play with us? Earl Fochette? I don't know.

Me, Alvin Alcone, Herbert Richardson. I don't know why it will come in my mind. Yeah. And, uh, Pete's brother played bass horn. I don't know why it will come in my mind. I don't know if Alvin can tell you. Cause he's young and mean and remembers. Yeah. And, uh, Pete's brother played bass horn with us. Henry. Yeah, Henry played bass horn with us. Henry. Yeah, Henry played bass horn with us. I believe Johnny Sincere played with us. I think. I think he did. I think Johnny Sincere played with us. I think Johnny Sincere played with us. I think he did. I think Johnny played with us. But Alvin can tell you. He, uh, Mm-hm.
What about, you said Steve sang some nasty songs.

He would play then, huh? Terrible. He would play then. See some white people would come in, you know, and request him to play some. And he'd come in and play. But I mean he'd come in and play with the band, you see. And then when they'd want to play them songs, them nasty songs, they wouldn't do it in the dance hall. And he'd be there by himself, you know, after the dance clothes, you know, see. And they'd sit there and he'd sing them songs from them. What about when you first came back from Texas? That's something I wanted to ask you about.
